expectations.text: End users prevented from granting consent to third-party OAuth applications — consent by an authorised administrator only (ISM-2137)
expectations.evidence: "End users prevented from consenting to third-party OAuth apps (admin-only) — ISM-2137... Only administrators may grant consent"

expectations.text: OAuth application consents reviewed at least every six months, revoking unused apps and excessive permissions (ISM-2138)
expectations.evidence: "Consents reviewed 6-monthly — ISM-2138... recurring 6-monthly cycle... Revoke grants for apps that fail the review" including scope-vs-justification checks

expectations.text: Central logging of consent grants, token issuance and token use (ISM-2139)
expectations.evidence: "Consent/token events centrally logged — ISM-2139... consent grant events and OAuth token issuance/refresh events must flow to central, tamper-evident logging"

expectations.text: OAuth device code flow disabled unless required; where required, restricted to authorised accounts and managed devices (ISM-2140)
expectations.evidence: "Device code flow disabled unless required — ISM-2140... disabled tenant-wide unless there is a documented business need... narrowly scoped exceptions... individually risk-assessed"

expectations.text: Frames why: consent phishing and token theft are current attack paths; ties to session/token binding and revocation controls in the same release
expectations.evidence: Frames consent phishing ("known phishing/consent-grant-attack vector") and token misuse alerting, but does not tie to the session/token binding and revocation controls (ISM-2141–2148) of the same release
